NOS integration is required to activate these, which the datasheet states with an asterisk against the whole timing block. The datasheet's introduction separately states IEEE 802.1CM fronthaul and ITU-T G.8273.2 T-BC Class C" data-gnss="internal receiver for master clock implementations" data-routing="full Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6)" data-roles="C-RAN hub 5G fronthaul transport aggregation; backhaul aggregation for BBU pooling; programmable as a Broadband Network Gateway (BNG)" data-optics-qsfp28="100G QSFP28 SR4/LR4/ER4/ZR4, up to 80 km per the HIG port table" data-optics-sfp28="25G SFP28 SR/LR/ER; 10G SFP+ SR/LR/ER; 1G SFP SX/LX/EX - the same cages take all three speeds, and the HIG's port table rates ports 0-63 to 40 km" data-timing-cables="the datasheet's Compatible Timing Cable Types row - 50 ohm SMA coaxial with a 1/4-36UNS-2B connector for GNSS; 50 ohm SMB coaxial with a 10-32UNF-2A connector for 1PPS and 10MHz; shielded RJ45 for ToD. The accessory kit ships two SMB-to-BNC converter cables" data-optics-sfp-plus="10G on the two SFP+ management ports. The datasheet's Compatible Transceiver Types list is one list for the whole box and names no management-only part, so the speed here is the port list's ('2 x 10G SFP+ management ports')" data-timing-interfaces="GNSS SMA in; 1PPS SMB in/out; 10MHz SMB in/out; ToD RJ45 in/out" data-console="RJ45 RS-232 plus a micro-USB serial console" data-oob="1x RJ45 100/1000M management port" data-safety="UL 62368-1; IEC 60950-1; IEC 62368-1; BSMI" data-emc="FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 55024; EN 55035; EN 62479; EN 50663; EN 300 386; EN 301 489; EN 303 413; BSMI; MTCTE; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A" data-nebs="NEBS GR-1089, GR-3108 (EMC); NEBS GR-63 (environment)" data-environment="ETSI 300 019; ETSI 300 132-2; RoHS; WEEE; MTCTE" data-eol="none-announced" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }

       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="609.6mm" height="87.7mm" viewBox="0 0 609.6 87.7" data-device="s9600-72xc" data-view="left" data-switching-capacity="2.4 Tbps" data-packet-buffer="4 GB deep buffer" data-power-typical-w="328" data-power-max-w="685" data-power-envelope="bare" data-input-ac="100 to 240 V, 12 A" data-input-dc="-40 to -75 V, 40 A" data-psu-redundancy="1+1 hot-swappable" data-fan-redundancy="3+1 hot-swappable" data-airflow="front-to-back" data-operating-temp="0 to 45 C" data-operating-humidity="5 to 85% RH non-condensing" data-storage-temp="-40 to 70 C" data-storage-humidity="5 to 93% RH non-condensing" data-asic="Broadcom Qumran2c BCM88820 with optional Broadcom OP2 BCM16K external TCAM (premium SKU only)" data-cpu="Intel Skylake-D 8-core @ 1.9 GHz" data-memory="32 GB DDR4 (up to 64 GB)" data-storage="128 GB SSD" data-bmc="ASPEED AST2400" data-timing="Stratum 3E OCXO with optional holdover; SyncE (ITU-T); IEEE 1588v2 default, G.8265.1, G.8275.1, G.8275.2, SMPTE ST 2059-2 (additional licence), T-GM, T-BC/OC, T-TC; Time Sensitive Networking (TSN); Class C timing accuracy. NOS integration is required to activate these, which the datasheet states with an asterisk against the whole timing block. The datasheet's introduction separately states IEEE 802.1CM fronthaul and ITU-T G.8273.2 T-BC Class C" data-gnss="internal receiver for master clock implementations" data-routing="full Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6)" data-roles="C-RAN hub 5G fronthaul transport aggregation; backhaul aggregation for BBU pooling; programmable as a Broadband Network Gateway (BNG)" data-optics-qsfp28="100G QSFP28 SR4/LR4/ER4/ZR4, up to 80 km per the HIG port table" data-optics-sfp28="25G SFP28 SR/LR/ER; 10G SFP+ SR/LR/ER; 1G SFP SX/LX/EX - the same cages take all three speeds, and the HIG's port table rates ports 0-63 to 40 km" data-timing-cables="the datasheet's Compatible Timing Cable Types row - 50 ohm SMA coaxial with a 1/4-36UNS-2B connector for GNSS; 50 ohm SMB coaxial with a 10-32UNF-2A connector for 1PPS and 10MHz; shielded RJ45 for ToD. The accessory kit ships two SMB-to-BNC converter cables" data-optics-sfp-plus="10G on the two SFP+ management ports. The datasheet's Compatible Transceiver Types list is one list for the whole box and names no management-only part, so the speed here is the port list's ('2 x 10G SFP+ management ports')" data-timing-interfaces="GNSS SMA in; 1PPS SMB in/out; 10MHz SMB in/out; ToD RJ45 in/out" data-console="RJ45 RS-232 plus a micro-USB serial console" data-oob="1x RJ45 100/1000M management port" data-safety="UL 62368-1; IEC 60950-1; IEC 62368-1; BSMI" data-emc="FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 55024; EN 55035; EN 62479; EN 50663; EN 300 386; EN 301 489; EN 303 413; BSMI; MTCTE; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A" data-nebs="NEBS GR-1089, GR-3108 (EMC); NEBS GR-63 (environment)" data-environment="ETSI 300 019; ETSI 300 132-2; RoHS; WEEE; MTCTE" data-eol="none-announced" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }

The datasheet's introduction separately states IEEE 802.1CM fronthaul and ITU-T G.8273.2 T-BC Class C" data-gnss="internal receiver for master clock implementations" data-routing="full Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6)" data-roles="C-RAN hub 5G fronthaul transport aggregation; backhaul aggregation for BBU pooling; programmable as a Broadband Network Gateway (BNG)" data-optics-qsfp28="100G QSFP28 SR4/LR4/ER4/ZR4, up to 80 km per the HIG port table" data-optics-sfp28="25G SFP28 SR/LR/ER; 10G SFP+ SR/LR/ER; 1G SFP SX/LX/EX - the same cages take all three speeds, and the HIG's port table rates ports 0-63 to 40 km" data-timing-cables="the datasheet's Compatible Timing Cable Types row - 50 ohm SMA coaxial with a 1/4-36UNS-2B connector for GNSS; 50 ohm SMB coaxial with a 10-32UNF-2A connector for 1PPS and 10MHz; shielded RJ45 for ToD. The accessory kit ships two SMB-to-BNC converter cables" data-optics-sfp-plus="10G on the two SFP+ management ports.   <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }

    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-132-ac@'] .state-input-lost { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-132-ac@'] .state-input-lost { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-132-ac@'] .state-ok { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-132-ac@'] .state-standby { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-132-ac@'] .state-standby { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }

    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-132-ac@'] .state-warning { animation: portrayal-alternate 1s linear infinite; }
</style>
